paragraphs: Shimon ben Tarfon. (A tanna mentioned in a baraita.)

Two legal teachings of his remain with us, as in [Shevuot 47b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.47b.3-4). He said: “This teaches that the oath takes effect upon both of them.” He also said there: “Where is the warning against one who acts as a procurer for an adulterer? Scripture says, ‘You shall not commit adultery’—read as ‘You shall not cause adultery.’”[^1][^2]

He also said there: “‘And you murmured in your tents’—you scouted [the land] and maligned [God] in the tent of the Omnipresent.” He also said there: “Draw near to one who is oiled, and be oiled yourself.”[^3]

notes.text: The source reads כשבועות מז:, “as in Shevuot 47b”; the initial kaf need not be changed to a bet to translate it. Hyman introduces “two legal teachings” and then adds two further sayings. All four sayings occur together in the checked William Davidson Hebrew text of Shevuot 47b:3–6. Their attribution there is Shimon ben Tarfon, without an added personal title.

The wordplay is לא תנאף / לא תנאיף, “do not commit adultery” / “do not cause adultery.” Hyman’s phrase העוקב אחר נואף is rendered with the checked Vilna Rashi on Shevuot 47b:4:1: the person acts as an agent arranging women for the adulterer. “Procurer” conveys that assisting role, rather than merely following someone physically.

Both verbs in תרתם וגיניתם are retained. The bracketed objects are explanatory glosses from the checked Vilna Rashi on Shevuot 47b:5:1–2: “you scouted” refers to the land, and “you maligned” to the Omnipresent who caused His presence to dwell among them. The phrase “in the tent of the Omnipresent” follows the underlying Hebrew wording; it is not a new claim that the people physically entered a sanctuary. Rashi on 47b:6:1 explains the oil proverb through contact with someone covered in oil and through the Euphrates gaining importance from its association with the Land of Israel. That context explains the image, but is not inserted into Hyman’s abbreviated quotation.
